content:
iPhone Duo is less than a month away from launch, but many prospective buyers still want to know how the device performs when used left-handed. The video below shows an example of left-handed use.

Here is a look at iPhone Duo being used left-handed.

If you're a left-handed user, the iPhone Duo may excite you, but it will also raise some questions. Because this new foldable device is clearly designed primarily for right-handed use.

When using the outer screen, the left side of the iPhone Duo has a straight edge, since that's where the hinge is located. But the right side has a rounded design, allowing you to open it up like a book.

The Dock row is also positioned on the right side of the screen, and Apple has not yet indicated whether it will offer an accessibility setting to let users move it to the left.

So what will the experience be like for left-handed users with the iPhone Duo?

Since everyone's hand size is different, you'll have to visit an Apple Store in person to find out the real answer. But I recently came across a video of someone using the iPhone Duo left-handed — it was the first time I'd seen anyone try it that way.

Below is a video from Tom Hitchins (@bytereview) on Instagram:

Hitchins looks a bit awkward using it, but he explained in the comments that he's actually a right-handed user, so his left-handed test was done on behalf of others.

The video is titled "good enough," since Hitchins can reach across from the left to the Dock row on the right. But it's best to try it yourself in person before deciding.

I'm a right-handed user, but I'm used to holding my iPhone with my left hand so that my dominant hand can be free to do other things. I imagine there are quite a few other right-handed users who do the same. So I'm a little uncertain about having to switch to holding the iPhone Duo with my right hand, but I'll share my thoughts once I've had a chance to try it.

Are you worried about using the iPhone Duo left-handed? Let us know in the comments.
